advice: Experiment: replace the n==512 call to `sera_libxsmm_512` with 16 calls to the existing `sera_libxsmm_panel32`, for row offsets r=0,32,...,480. For each call set parameters[4]=B, parameters[10]=A+r*512, and parameters[16]=C+r*512; leave other fields zero. This changes the packed A panel from 64 rows (128 KiB, 256-byte K stride) to 32 rows (64 KiB, 128-byte K stride). The hypothesis is that the smaller scratch footprint may reduce cache-capacity or set-conflict pressure on the M4 Pro; this is unverified and does not establish a cache cause. Keep the non-512 fallback unchanged and include all 16 calls, packing, allocation, SME transitions, and stores in timing.
risks: Sixteen helper calls add call and SME entry/exit overhead, and the helper’s narrower panel may not offset that cost. Do not add padding to this experiment: the supplied helper has fixed generated strides, and padding would require coordinated generated-code and allocation changes. Check the full GEMM at n=512 and the existing general-size, tail, n<=0, and tolerance cases; confirm the 16 row bands cover C exactly with no overlap or gaps. Measure with fresh paired controls under the unchanged hill and power settings, report spread, and make no causal claim from noisy scores. No speedup is established.
